answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying reputation to verifiable work rather than to identity claims. Picture an orchard where each tree must be tended season by season: an agent earns standing only by completing attested tasks over time, so a fresh fake identity starts with nothing. A single ember of trust, one attestation from a peer, cannot unlock high-value work; the agent must build a history of useful contributions. That history becomes its haven: privileges grow with proven behavior, while dishonest identities lose their standing and start over, making mass fakes expensive.
